subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared schema-visible metadata field to opaque channel group entries, and should the canonical field be `label`?
rationale: This creates permanent public configuration surface across multiple channel owners; JSON5 comments and resolver commands do not settle the field semantics, naming, or exact scope.

options.title: Standardize `label`
options.body: Add one optional inert `label` string to applicable opaque-ID entry schemas, types, metadata, tests, and documentation without using it for routing or authorization.

options.title: Use `description`
options.body: Add a more general optional `description` string, accepting a more verbose configuration shape and weaker identity semantics.

options.title: Keep current tools
options.body: Decline new configuration surface and document JSON5 comments plus supported channel name-resolution commands as the readability workflow.

recommendation.title: Standardize `label`
recommendation.body: Add one optional inert `label` string to applicable opaque-ID entry schemas, types, metadata, tests, and documentation without using it for routing or authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-channel public config-contract decision, and the product-ownership and schema-history evidence points most strongly here.
